summary: The PJM Transmission Owners file tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in a new docket, ER27-520-000. The filing sets rates for the new co-located and large-load services, a pro forma cost recovery agreement with a minimum revenue commitment and credit support, and a 15-year zonal allocation of upgrade costs from PJM’s Fast Energization Process.
ask: Accept the tariff revisions without hearing, modification or condition, with the new service rates effective March 16, 2027 and the agreement and cost allocation on an indeterminate date.

points.point: The owners say the revisions answer the E-7 show cause order and comply with the E-2 co-location order.
points.quote: These revisions are both responsive to and consistent with the preliminary findings made by the Commission in its June 18, 2026 Order Instituting Proceeding

points.point: Large Load customers would make a minimum contribution to transmission revenue requirements, backed by shortfall payments and financial security.
points.quote: to make a minimum contribution towards transmission owners’ revenue requirements, along with a shortfall payment and crediting mechanism and financial security obligations

points.point: The committed contribution is 80% to 100% of a full firm transmission service benchmark.
points.quote: which percentage shall be no less than 80% and no greater than 100%

points.point: Initial credit support equals the projected charges on the full initial load commitment over the agreement’s term.
points.quote: equals the aggregate projected charges associated with 100 percent of the Initial Load Commitment over the CRA term

points.point: The cost recovery agreement runs at least ten years after the first service date.
points.quote: the date that is at least ten (10) years after the first Service Date as specified in Exhibit A

points.point: Owners may keep using existing or new customer protections instead of the pro forma agreement if FERC accepts them.
points.quote: as alternatives to the pro forma CRA, so long as those arrangements result in comparable protections and are accepted for filing by the Commission

points.point: Upgrade costs from Fast Energization go to the zones with large loads for 15 years, then to regional allocation.
points.quote: this allocation methodology will apply to each portfolio of IRRs identified through PJM’s Fast Energization Process for 15 years

points.point: Rates for the three new transmission services largely repeat those FERC approved in the co-location order.
points.quote: The rates for these services are largely identical to those proposed by the PJM Transmission Owners and approved by the Commission in the Co-Located Load Paper Hearing Order

points.point: The owners commit to change their formula rate templates to show state regulators the costs of transmission built for large loads.
points.quote: provide transparency to state regulators and other interested parties regarding the costs of transmission facilities being constructed by each Transmission Owner to provide transmission service to Large Loads

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 to answer the E-7 show cause order for PJM. The owners also say it meets their compliance obligation under the E-2 co-location order and will tell the EL25-49 parties so by letter.
